findings: SEC documentation independently confirms that most leveraged and inverse ETFs reset daily and obtain exposure through swaps, futures and other derivatives.
Direxion independently states that its leveraged/inverse ETFs rebalance exposure daily by buying or selling swaps and that target exposure is a function of target leverage and net assets.
The frozen causal premise therefore survives at the product-mandate level: daily target maintenance creates recurring exposure adjustment.

The stronger frozen claim that sign and rough market-wide scale can be derived point-in-time before the close is not yet established. Historical pre-close AUM/shares, same-day creations/redemptions, product benchmark mappings and net long/inverse exposure must be reconstructed without using post-close NAV or holdings.

Derivative implementation transfers hedge demand to swap/futures counterparties; opposing products can offset and dealer pre-hedging can alter timing. Gross fund reset arithmetic therefore cannot be represented as executable constituent demand without a separately frozen mapping and netting model.
No price, return or economic outcome was inspected.
required_reopen_conditions: Demonstrate a reproducible historical PIT source for each included product's shares/AUM that is known before the expression freeze time.
Version leverage targets and benchmark mappings historically.
Freeze ex ante treatment of creations/redemptions, long/inverse netting and derivatives-to-benchmark exposure mapping.
Define a pre-close freeze clock that cannot consume same-day closing NAV or post-close holdings.
Declare cost/capacity model before any authorized economic test.
claim_restriction: Retain only that daily-reset leveraged/inverse products create rules-based exposure adjustments. Do not claim that public pre-close inputs currently identify executable net close flow, price pressure, or economic edge.
